chapter01Description: Every clock in the Meridian House has stopped. Find Elias Vale's last night — and the way out.
clueApprenticeBody: Elias Vale, apprenticed to the Meridian Guild — 1874.
clueAstrolabeBody: First the guide sailors steer by, then the mirror that borrows its light, then the key that turns what sleeps, then the flame that needs no spark.
clueBlueprintBody: Lower-left VENT SEQUENCE: up, down, up, down. Upper-right CABINET CODE — count teeth, small gear first: 24, 36.
clueBookDatesBody: Three spines: 1861, 1874, 1892. The shelf plate reads: earliest first.
clueClock1024Body: The grandfather clock's hands rest at 10:24.
clueDialOrderBody: Orrery order — Gallery time, then Study time, then Workshop time; the year last.
clueDoormatBody: Wax where the moon hides — up, down, up.
clueEhSecretBody: Light returns to those who set the flames right.
clueEpilogueBody: The observatory was sealed the night the Meridian Star aligned. The mechanism I protected is still running — somewhere. If you are reading this, the house has chosen you next. — E.V.
clueGaLetterBody: What turns guards the left frame; what guides the center; what waxes the right.
clueMarksOrderBody: Carved left to right: moon, then star, then sun.
clueMoonPhasesBody: The moon writes its name in order: new, crescent, half, full.
cluePortraitDatesBody: Medallion plaques: 1802, 1827, 1851, 1868. Gallery rule: the dead keep their places — earliest at the left.
clueRegulatorBody: Wound, the regulator ticks once and stops: 03:47.
clueSampleLockOpenedBody: Inside the panel: a second, smaller lock.
clueSampleNoteBody: The clockmaker wrote: 'Time is a lock, not a river.'
clueSealPhraseBody: SEALED BY E.V. — THE MERIDIAN KEEPS WHAT IT IS GIVEN.
clueSealYearBody: Sealed in the year of the Meridian transit: 1892.
clueValeLetterBody: Turn the world until the line that remembers faces the flame.
clueValeNote1Body: The archive keeps what the house forgets. — E.V.
clueValeNote2Body: Vale's apprenticeship record, 1874 — guild seals still attached.
clueValeNote3Body: The frame is for something that looks far — keep it polished.
clueValeNote4Body: The last night: he set every clock to stop at a piece of the truth, and trusted the house to keep it until someone cared enough to look.
clueWkClockBody: Once powered, the wall clock still shows where it died: 06:58.
combFocusLensResult: The lens seats into the brass frame with a click: a focusing lens.
combinationSampleHookMessage: You fit the gear onto the key, making a hooked tool.
hint.puz_eh_door_lock.l1: The house keeps time in its own way. One clock here never stopped — it just forgot how to start again.
hint.puz_eh_door_lock.l2: Inspect the large clock on the left wall. Its hands point to a time — that time is the code.
hint.puz_eh_door_lock.l3: The grandfather clock stopped at 10:24. Enter 1-0-2-4 on the door panel.
hint.puz_eh_marks.l1: Someone carved a message beside the door. Whatever order they carved it in — that's the answer.
hint.puz_eh_marks.l2: Inspect the marks closely: moon first, then star, then sun. Set the dials in that order, left to right.
hint.puz_eh_marks.l3: Dial 1 = moon, dial 2 = star, dial 3 = sun. Then pull the brass lever.
hint.puz_eh_sconce.l1: The doormat is heavier than it looks.
hint.puz_eh_sconce.l2: Lift the doormat and read the note. It describes which flames should burn.
hint.puz_eh_sconce.l3: Note says: up, down, up. Set switch 1 up, switch 2 down, switch 3 up.
hint.puz_ga_case_lock.l1: Whose reliquary is this? Whose year would it keep?
hint.puz_ga_case_lock.l2: The central portrait was just revealed. Read the birth year on its inscription.
hint.puz_ga_frames.l1: The letter doesn't name symbols — it names jobs.
hint.puz_ga_frames.l2: What turns is the key, what guides is the star, what waxes is the moon. Left, center, right.
hint.puz_ga_frames.l3: Left: key. Center: star. Right: moon.
hint.puz_ga_moon_dial.l1: The astrolabe note ended with the moon's order. The Study remembers it.
hint.puz_ga_moon_dial.l2: Revisit the astrolabe clue: new, crescent, half, full — positions 1 to 4.
hint.puz_ga_moon_dial.l3: Dial 1: new moon. 2: crescent. 3: half. 4: full.
hint.puz_ga_portraits.l1: Every brass plaque has a year. Time only runs one way in a gallery.
hint.puz_ga_portraits.l2: Read the plaque years — 1802, 1827, 1851, 1868 — earliest at the left.
hint.puz_ob_orrery.l1: Three clocks in this house kept their stopping times. The chart tells you the order.
hint.puz_ob_orrery.l2: Journal clues: regulator 03:47, wall clock 06:58, chronometer 08:15, seal year 1892. Chart order: gallery, study, workshop — then the year.
hint.puz_ob_orrery.l3: Enter 0-8-1-5, then 0-3-4-7, then 0-6-5-8, then year 1-8-9-2. Keep the leading zeros!
hint.puz_ob_starchart.l1: The chart isn't decoration — it has a path drawn through it.
hint.puz_ob_starchart.l2: Follow the dotted line. Each constellation carries a small sigil: frame, key, gear.
hint.puz_ob_starchart.l3: Tap in path order: frame (Gallery), then key (Study), then gear (Workshop).
hint.puz_ob_telescope.l1: The lens was made for this. The star was waiting for it.
hint.puz_ob_telescope.l2: Combine lens and frame in your satchel into the focusing lens, fit it here, then find the circled star.
hint.puz_ob_telescope.l3: Rotate to about 150 degrees until the crosshair sits on the ink-circled star.
hint.puz_st_astrolabe.l1: Vale described the rings without naming them. Every symbol has a job.
hint.puz_st_astrolabe.l2: Sailors steer by the star; the moon borrows the sun's light; the key turns the lock; the sun needs no spark. Match the descriptions, outermost ring first.
hint.puz_st_astrolabe.l3: Outer to inner: star, moon, key, sun.
hint.puz_st_books.l1: Vale was a man of dates. Every book on this shelf has one.
hint.puz_st_books.l2: Read the years on the spines — 1861, 1874, 1892 — and follow the label: earliest first.
hint.puz_st_books.l3: Place the 1861 book left, the 1874 book middle, the 1892 book right.
hint.puz_st_globe.l1: The desk note says the world must face the flame.
hint.puz_st_globe.l2: Find the red meridian line and the small brass pointer. Turn until they meet.
hint.puz_st_globe.l3: Rotate the globe about 210 degrees — the red line should point at the pointer.
hint.puz_st_safe.l1: Guild records are proud of their years.
hint.puz_st_safe.l2: The framed certificate on the wall names a year — Vale's apprenticeship. That year opens the box.
hint.puz_wk_code.l1: The cabinet doesn't want a word. It wants numbers the gears already know.
hint.puz_wk_code.l2: Blueprint, upper-right: tooth counts, small gear first — 24 then 36.
hint.puz_wk_crane.l1: The crane is hungry for a handle, and patient for an angle.
hint.puz_wk_crane.l2: The parts cabinet held a winch handle. Fit it, then follow the chalk arrow on the floor.
hint.puz_wk_crane.l3: Rotate the arm to about 300 degrees so the hook reaches the X-marked crate.
hint.puz_wk_floorboard.l1: One board in this floor wasn't laid by the same hands.
hint.puz_wk_floorboard.l2: Look for the board that sits slightly higher, with a clean gap where dust can't settle.
hint.puz_wk_floorboard.l3: The middle row, second board from the left — tap it firmly.
hint.puz_wk_gears.l1: Three rings, three markers, one pointer each.
hint.puz_wk_gears.l2: Turn each ring until its brass mark reaches the small pointer at the top.
hint.puz_wk_gears.l3: Ring A: 0 degrees, ring B: 120 degrees, ring C: 240 degrees — all markers at top.
hint.puz_wk_levers.l1: The blueprint on the wall has more than one diagram on it.
hint.puz_wk_levers.l2: Check the lower-left corner of the blueprint — a small VENT SEQUENCE diagram shows four positions.
hint.puz_wk_levers.l3: Up, down, up, down — levers 1 through 4.
hotEhPaintingDesc: A townhouse under a night sky. The signature has worn away.
hotEhWindowDesc: Beyond the glass, the street is asleep. The latch is sealed shut.
hotObExitDoorDesc: The house's front door. Chains of brass run through its handles — Vale sealed it himself. Something still ticks behind the walls.
hotStRegulatorDesc: It hasn't run in years — a winding keyhole gleams under the dial.
hotspotSampleHookPanelDesc: A brass panel carved with a gear and a key.
hotspotSampleNoteDesc: A folded note lies on the desk.
itemClockKeyDesc: A brass key sized for regulator movements.
itemCrankDesc: A heavy crank for the hoist.
itemFocusDesc: Lens in frame — it makes far things close enough to read.
itemFrameDesc: A precision ring frame, machined for that lens.
itemLensDesc: A plain lens, chipped at one edge. It wants a frame.
itemSampleGearDesc: A single gear from an old mechanism.
itemSampleHookDesc: A combined tool: key mounted on a gear.
itemSampleKeyDesc: A small brass key, still warm.
puz.puz_eh_door_lock.instr: Enter the 4-digit code that opens the study door.
puz.puz_eh_door_lock.title: The Sealed Study Door
puz.puz_eh_marks.instr: Reproduce the carved symbol sequence on the three dials.
puz.puz_eh_marks.title: Marks Beside the Door
puz.puz_eh_sconce.instr: Flip the three sconce switches to match the pattern noted under the doormat.
puz.puz_eh_sconce.title: The Dark Sconces
puz.puz_ga_case_lock.instr: Open the reliquary with its 4-digit code.
puz.puz_ga_case_lock.title: The Reliquary
puz.puz_ga_frames.instr: Set the three empty frames' symbols as Vale's letter describes.
puz.puz_ga_frames.title: Empty Frames
puz.puz_ga_moon_dial.instr: Set the moon dial so the four phases sit in Vale's order.
puz.puz_ga_moon_dial.title: The Moon Dial
puz.puz_ga_portraits.instr: Hang the four portrait medallions in chronological order.
puz.puz_ga_portraits.title: The Gallery Order
puz.puz_ob_orrery.instr: Set the three time rings and the year ring to the stopped times, in the star chart's order. Keep every leading zero!
puz.puz_ob_orrery.title: The Orrery
puz.puz_ob_starchart.instr: Tap the three marked constellations in the order the dotted path draws them.
puz.puz_ob_starchart.title: The Star Chart
puz.puz_ob_telescope.instr: With the focusing lens mounted, turn the telescope until its crosshair rests on the circled star.
puz.puz_ob_telescope.title: The Last Lens
puz.puz_st_astrolabe.instr: Align the astrolabe's four rings so the pointer reads Vale's intended sequence, outermost first.
puz.puz_st_astrolabe.title: The Astrolabe
puz.puz_st_books.instr: Return three fallen books to the shelf in the order Vale intended. The shelf label says: earliest first.
puz.puz_st_books.title: The Stopped Hours
puz.puz_st_globe.instr: Rotate the globe until its marked meridian aligns with the brass pointer.
puz.puz_st_globe.title: The Meridian Globe
puz.puz_st_safe.instr: Open the strongbox with its 4-digit combination.
puz.puz_st_safe.title: Vale's Strongbox
puz.puz_wk_code.title: The Parts Cabinet
puz.puz_wk_crane.instr: With the winch handle fitted, swing the crane arm until the hook catches the X-marked crate.
puz.puz_wk_crane.title: The Hoist Crane
puz.puz_wk_floorboard.instr: Find the loose floorboard among its neighbors and lift it.
puz.puz_wk_floorboard.title: The Loose Floorboard
puz.puz_wk_gears.instr: Rotate the three gear rings until each marked tooth sits at the top pointer.
puz.puz_wk_gears.title: The Frozen Gear Train
puz.puz_wk_levers.instr: Set the four levers to the pattern on Vale's blueprint.
puz.puz_wk_levers.title: The Lever Board
puzzleSampleLockHint1: Look around the room for digits.
puzzleSampleLockHint2: The plaque by the door shows the first two digits.
roomEntranceDescription: Cold light through tall windows. One grandfather clock looms over the door.
roomGalleryDescription: Portraits in gilt frames, and three that hang empty.
roomObservatoryDescription: A dome of brass stars, an orrery, and one circled light.
roomSampleDescription: A minimal room used to validate the content pipeline.
roomStudyDescription: A cluttered desk, a stopped regulator, certificates on the wall.
roomWorkshopDescription: Half-assembled machines under a frozen gear train.
